component.name: whatsapp
component.title: WhatsApp
component.description: Send messages to WhatsApp, and receive its events in webhook mode.
component.label: cloud,api,chat

phoneNumberId.description: Phone Number ID taken from WhatsApp Meta for Developers Dashboard

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

baseUri.label: advanced
baseUri.description: Can be used to set an alternative base URI, e.g. when you want to test the component against a mock WhatsApp API

authorizationToken.label: security
authorizationToken.description: Authorization Token taken from WhatsApp Meta for Developers Dashboard

CamelWhatsAppPhoneNumberId.label: producer
CamelWhatsAppPhoneNumberId.description: Phone Number ID taken from WhatsApp Meta for Developers Dashboard

CamelWhatsAppRecipientPhoneNumberId.label: producer
CamelWhatsAppRecipientPhoneNumberId.description: Recipient phone number associated with Phone Number ID

consumerOut.description: In webhook mode (webhook:whatsapp:...), the event that WhatsApp posts, as JSON text. The verification request of WhatsApp (a GET) also reaches the route, with the hub.challenge as the body when hub.mode is subscribe and hub.verify_token matches webhookVerifyToken, else with no body (403, or 400 when the parameters are missing). With webhookSecret, an event without a valid X-Hub-Signature-256 is answered with 403 and does not reach the route

consumerReply.description: The body at the end of the route is not sent: the reply is the body the route got, the event or the hub.challenge

producerIn.description: A request of org.apache.camel.component.whatsapp.model: a TextMessageRequest, MediaMessageRequest, LocationMessageRequest, ContactMessageRequest, InteractiveMessageRequest or TemplateMessageRequest to send a message, or an UploadMediaRequest to upload a media file. Text, bytes, a Map or another POJO fails: build the request. No body sends nothing

producerOut.description: The org.apache.camel.component.whatsapp.model.MessageResponse of WhatsApp, with the ids of the messages sent, or the id of the media uploaded. No body is left as it is

phoneNumberId.description: The phone number ID taken from whatsapp-business dashboard.

exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

authorizationToken.label: security
authorizationToken.description: The authorization access token taken from whatsapp-business dashboard.

webhookSecret.label: security
webhookSecret.description: The app secret used to verify the X-Hub-Signature-256 signature of inbound webhook event payloads (from the Meta/WhatsApp app dashboard). When set, event callbacks with a missing or invalid signature are rejected with HTTP 403; when not set, no signature verification is performed.
